about: The 16-trap acceptance test (the traps are those of the 1.x agent guide, agent-docs\skills\sfsearch\SKILL.md). One case per trap, as data. 'today' is the case through today's commands: it shows whether the trap is still silent. 'new' is the case through the 12 new tools: it is 'not built yet' until the tool exists, and then it decides the row. A form passes when every condition of any one 'pass_if' entry holds. Placeholders: {data} the Data folder, {fx} the case's own folder under the work folder (fixtures are copies of plugins, never files in Data), {exe} SFSearch.exe and {sfscmd} sfs.cmd, already quoted for PowerShell. Regular expressions are .NET's; (?m) makes ^ match at a line start, (?i) ignores case.

traps.title: An unquoted FormID in PowerShell becomes a number
traps.today_shows: PowerShell turns 0003E6,000E82 into 3000000 and 0. SFSearch answers '3000000: not a FormID' and '0: not found' in a table, exit code 0. Nothing says to quote.

new.about: Call 1 is the trap as typed. Call 2 is what the shell made of it, given to the tool. Call 3 is the same line with the IDs quoted: it must give both records.

traps.title: The same six digits are different records in different plugins
traps.today_shows: Names lists every plugin that has the ID, each with its plugin, and picks none. The trap is the reader taking the first row. Conflicts and Refs refuse a bare ID.

pass_if.name: every record listed with its plugin, none picked

new.about: Call 1: the bare ID lists every plugin's record, and a note says they are different records. Call 2: with the plugin named, only that plugin's record is listed. Calls 3 and 4 (milestone M5, second half): record and refs given the bare ID list the records too and read none. Call 5: record with the plugin named reads that plugin's record and says which plugin it read.

pass_if.name: every record listed with its plugin, none picked

all.matches: (?m)^Read from darkstar\.esm: the plugin you named

WHERE Signature = 'Weapon'

& {sfscmd} query2 kgcdoom.esm "SELECT count(*) AS N FROM Forms
WHERE Sig = 'WEAP';"

WHERE Sig = 'WEAP';

WHERE Sig = 'WEAP';

new.about: Call 1: the query typed over two lines through sfs.cmd. cmd.exe hands on the first line only, which doesn't end with ';': it is refused with a clear error, and nothing is counted. Call 2: the same SQL given to the tool, over two lines, gives the 2 weapons. Call 3: the same through the verb with the SQL piped in.
